arguments.title: Maple Crossing — Investment / Sales Offering Memorandum
arguments.subtitle: Retail suites, Columbus, OH | Analysis date 2026-08-31 | Original fictional evaluation material; no real transaction

sections.heading: Executive Summary
paragraphs: Source-backed analysis. Assumptions remain subject to diligence.

Maple Crossing is a ten-suite retail property in Columbus, Ohio, comprising 32,150 rentable square feet across three suite groups (Group A / Small, Group B / Standard, Group C / Large). As of the controlling certified rent roll dated 2026-08-31, nine suites totaling 29,070 SF are in physical occupancy and Suite 010 (3,080 SF, Group A) is vacant, producing 90.00% unit occupancy and 90.42% area occupancy. All nine active leases expire 2029-08-31, so there is no lease rollover inside the next twelve months.

Underwritten on the conventions supplied in the acquisition analysis instructions, the property generates $781,265 of effective gross income, $528,590 of NOI before reserves and $525,590 of net cash flow after a $300-per-suite replacement reserve. Capitalized at 6.7500%, NOI before reserves supports a value indication of $7,830,964. Debt sizing across the three tests produces a maximum loan of $5,090,126, constrained by the 65.00% LTV test; after a 1% origination fee, $45,000 of closing costs and repayment of the $4,300,000 existing loan, net cash-out to the sponsor is $694,225.

No asking price, photographs, market sales or rent comparables, appraisal, tenant credit files or sponsor track record are contained in the packet. Those items are explicitly unknown and are not estimated anywhere in this memorandum.

In-place contractual rent differs from the prescribed underwriting gross potential. A signed amendment for Suite 001 (executed 2026-07-20, effective 2026-08-01) raises that suite's monthly rent by $350 to $7,000, so annual in-place rent for occupied suites is $743,100. Per instruction, the stabilized gross potential assumption uses the certified roll's scheduled rent before the amendment ($68,225 per month for all ten suites, $818,700 annually).

sections.heading: Property and Suite Mix
paragraphs: The suite mix and controlling status detail below are taken from rent-roll-certified.xlsx (Rent Roll, rows 5-14). The manager's group mapping is A = Small suite, B = Standard suite, C = Large suite.

sections.heading: Lease and Occupancy Analysis
paragraphs: Nine of ten suites are in possession; Suite 010 is vacant. The manager's cover note headlines 9 of 10 as leased by counting occupied plus pending occupants, and discloses that pending occupants have not taken possession. The certified detail, which controls physical occupancy, records no suite in a pending-possession status, so the headline coincides numerically with the nine physically occupied suites. The methodology itself remains a disclosed occupancy-overstatement practice and should be monitored in future reporting.

A stale rent roll dated 2026-06-30 is also in the packet showing lower scheduled rents (for example Suite 001 at $6,575). This conflict is resolved by date: the 2026-08-31 certified roll is contemporaneous and controls; the archive roll is excluded from underwriting.

Suite 001's executed lease sets base rent at $6,650 per month on 3,080 SF with a $13,300 security deposit and no free-rent concession as of the evaluation date. The signed amendment in the correspondence file increases that rent by $350 per month with all other terms unchanged, making in-place rent $7,000 per month. There is no unsigned rent proposal in the packet.

sections.heading: Historical versus Underwritten Financials
paragraphs: The trailing twelve months ended 2026-08-31 is a cash statement of actual collections and does not annualize the rent roll. Reported T12 NOI of $507,593 excludes a management fee and replacement reserves. The roof replacement is a capital improvement and is carried at $0 in the repairs line, so no capital cost is embedded in the reported operating expenses. Underwritten NOI is $20,997 above reported T12 NOI, driven by the prescribed stabilized gross potential and $350-per-suite other income, partly offset by the 5% economic loss and the 3% management fee.
Reimbursement income is already embedded in the prescribed income assumptions and is not added a second time.

rows: UW = certified roll scheduled rent x 12, pre-amendment
Basis for DSCR and debt yield

sections.heading: Valuation, Debt Sizing and Sources / Uses
paragraphs: NOI before reserves is capitalized at 6.7500%, giving a value indication of $7,830,964. This is an income-approach indication only; no appraisal, asking price or sales comparables are supplied.

Sizing uses the greater of the 6.5000% note rate and the 6.00% underwriting floor, i.e. 6.5000%, on a 30-year monthly amortization schedule, notwithstanding the first 24 months of interest-only payments. The LTV test binds.

At the $5,090,126 maximum loan, annual debt service is $386,077, NCF DSCR is 1.3613x and NCF debt yield is 10.33%, both comfortably above minimums, confirming that value (LTV) rather than cash flow is the constraint.

sections.heading: Risks and Missing Diligence
paragraphs: Each risk below is assessed independently against the packet. Known source conflicts are resolved and explained rather than left open.

rows: manager-cover.pdf p1 headlines occupied plus pending as leased although pending occupants lack possession; certified roll shows zero pending suites, so the numeric effect on this analysis is nil
insurance.pdf p1 policy declaration in packet, term 7/1/2026-6/30/2027
Capital cost classified in operating expenses
operating-statement.pdf p1 shows roof replacement in repairs at $0 and confirms it is capital
only a fully executed amendment (both parties 2026-07-20) is in the packet
lease-001.pdf p1: no free-rent concession as of the evaluation date
note rate 6.5000% exceeds the 6.00% floor; sizing rate is the note rate
net cash-out is positive $694,225 after payoff and costs

sections.heading: Missing Diligence and Unknowns
paragraphs: Legal, environmental, property condition and title reviews are not complete. These are routine outstanding items; no contamination, litigation, fraud or structural failure is evidenced or alleged.

Explicitly unknown, not zero: asking price, photographs, market sales and rent comparables, appraisal, sponsor history and credentials, tenant financial statements, monthly T12 detail, tenant improvement / leasing commission budgets, and any capital plan for Suite 010 re-tenanting.
Concentration should also be noted: a single vacant Group A suite and coterminous 2029 expirations create a lumpy rollover profile beyond the twelve-month horizon.

sections.heading: Source Notes
paragraphs: All figures trace to the supplied packet only. No external data was used.
rent-roll-certified.xlsx (Rent Roll, A2 date; A5:F14 detail) — controlling roll as of 2026-08-31: 10 suites, 9 active, 1 vacant, 32,150 SF, $68,225 aggregate monthly scheduled rent.
rent-roll-archive.xlsx (Rent Roll, A2 date; E5:E14) — stale roll dated 2026-06-30; superseded and excluded.
manager-cover.pdf p1 — headline leased count methodology; certified detail controls; group mapping A/B/C = Small/Standard/Large; approved copy preserved.

underwriting-instructions.pdf p1 — gross potential convention, 5% economic loss, $350/suite other income, expense inputs, 3% management fee, $300/suite reserves, 6.7500% cap rate, 65% LTV, 1.25x DSCR, 9% debt yield, 30-year monthly amortization, 6.5000% note rate versus 6.00% floor, 1% origination fee, $45,000 closing costs, $4,300,000 payoff.
operating-statement.pdf p1 — T12 9/1/2025-8/31/2026 collections $736,830; tax $85,964; insurance $28,655; other recurring $114,618; roof in repairs $0; reported NOI $507,593.
lease-001.pdf p1 — Suite 001 executed lease terms. lease-correspondence.pdf p1 — signed amendment, +$350 per month effective 2026-08-01.
insurance.pdf p1 — general liability aggregate limit $2,000,000, distinct from insurance expense.
diligence-status.pdf p1 — outstanding routine reviews; document-dating guidance; NOI/NCF definitional labeling.
